_note: Invented sample data for the app's demo mode. Not anyone's real workouts.

settings_schema.label: The butler is on holiday
settings_schema.help: Switch on when you are travelling or resting on purpose. The butler stops reviewing workouts and will not send any "where have you been" notes. Approving or declining his proposals still works.

settings_schema.label: Automatic weight change, up to
settings_schema.help: On routines you let him tune, weight changes this size or smaller happen on their own. Bigger ones wait for your approval. Set to 0 to approve every weight change yourself.

settings_schema.label: ...and no more than
settings_schema.help: A second limit for automatic weight changes, as a share of the current weight. Whichever limit is stricter wins. He never makes a lift more than 10% harder at once, whatever you set here.

settings_schema.label: Automatic rep change, up to
settings_schema.help: Changes to your rep target this size or smaller happen on their own. Bigger ones wait for you.

settings_schema.label: Automatic rest change, up to
settings_schema.help: Changes to the rest timer this size or smaller happen on their own. Bigger ones wait for you.

settings_schema.label: Most changes per workout
settings_schema.help: The most routine changes he may suggest after one workout, automatic and proposed together. Advice does not count. Set to 0 and he will only advise.

settings_schema.label: A lift has stalled after
settings_schema.help: If a lift has not beaten its earlier best in this many sessions, he calls it stalled and suggests a fix.

settings_schema.label: Sessions he studies per lift
settings_schema.help: How many past sessions of each lift he reads before giving his view, and how many the app charts. More history means steadier judgement and a slightly higher Claude bill.

settings_schema.label: Claude model

choices.label: Haiku 5.5 (about a quarter of a cent a workout)

settings_schema.help: The mind behind the butler's reviews. Sonnet is quick, sharp and thrifty. Opus is the senior consultant: a little wiser on tricky plateaus, at about twice the price. Haiku is the junior footman: very quick and almost free, a touch less shrewd. Your questions to the butler always use Haiku.

issues.title: 🎩 A proposal regarding Full Body 2
issues.body:
Your Grace,

The seated row has settled in at 130 lb for six sessions. A short step back usually breaks the jam, and as it is a bigger change than the house rules let me make alone, it awaits your word.

**I would not presume to make these changes without your word:**

- **Seated Row (Machine): 3 x 10 at 120 lb for two weeks, then back to 130 lb**. Stuck at 130 lb for six sessions. A short step back usually breaks the jam.

Reply **/approve** to carry on, or **/decline** and I shall say no more of it. (The ledger app has buttons for both.)

messages.question: What does 'stalled' mean in the ledger?
messages.answer:
Sir, a lift is stalled when your best effort has not moved for three sessions in a row.

It is not a reproach. It usually means the body has caught up with the work and wants a change: a little more rest, a short step back, or a different rep range.

messages.question: And slipping?
messages.answer:
Slipping, Sir, means your recent best is lower than it was. Your lateral raise is the one to watch: 20 lb for 11 a month ago, 15 lb for 10 now.

With your note about the shoulder, holding steady is the right call.

messages.question: Is my pull-up getting better? The numbers go down.
messages.answer:
Very much so, Sir. On the assisted pull-up the weight is help from the machine, so a smaller number means you are lifting more of yourself.

You began in September with 100 lb of help. On your last visit it was 70 lb for 8. That is thirty pounds of you that the machine no longer carries.

messages.question: How many workouts this month?
messages.answer: Nine so far in October, Sir, against eleven in September. The week of the 5th was the quiet one; since then you have kept to two or three a week.

messages.question: Why has my seated row stalled, and what would you change?
messages.answer:
Your Grace, I went back through every row you have logged before answering.

You reached 130 lb on Sep 12 and have done it seven times since, always for 8 or 9, never 10. The weight is not the trouble; the order and the rest are. The row comes straight after the pull-ups, when your back is already tired, and the timer says about a minute between sets.

I would change three things, in this order. Rest two full minutes between sets. Do the row first on the days it appears, before the pull-ups. And if all three sets still won't reach 10 in a fortnight, step back to 120 lb for 3 × 10 for two weeks, then return to 130 lb. I have written the last of these up for your approval under Awaiting.

accounts.title: Your Grace
accounts.headline: A sound month on the books, Your Grace: the legs are strong, and the arms are owed a visit.
accounts.summary:
Eleven workouts in September against eight in August, and not one week missed. That alone is the making of a month. The leg press rose from 270 lb to 290 lb for ten, the chest press from 100 lb to 120 lb, and the pull-up now asks for 10 lb less help than it did on the 4th.

The ledger is not all credit. The seated row reached 130 lb in the second week and has stayed there, and the assisted dips have not moved since the first. Biceps had no direct work at all: Hevy Trainer has been cutting the last exercise of the long days, and the last exercise is usually the arms.
highlights: Eleven workouts, the most in any month so far.
Leg press: 290 lb for 10, up from 270 lb.
Pull-up: down to 90 lb of help, from 100 lb.

balance.note: 30 sets of quadriceps, and every one of them earned.
Plenty of pulling; the row simply needs a new approach.
18 sets, up from 10, and the lateral raise climbing.
No curls at all this month, and the dips come last when the arms are spent.

stalls.cause: Six sessions at 130 lb with the reps wandering between 8 and 9. The rest between sets has been about a minute: too short for the heaviest pull of the day.
stalls.remedy: Rest a full two minutes, and stay at 130 lb until all three sets reach 10. If nothing moves in two weeks, spend a fortnight at 120 lb for 3 × 10.

stalls.cause: 60 lb of help since the first week, done last in the workout when the arms have nothing left.
stalls.remedy: Do them before the curls rather than after, and reach 10 reps before asking for less help. Then 55 lb.

trainer_settings.why: Most September workouts ran 55 to 62 minutes against a 45-minute setting, so Trainer has been dropping the last exercise.
Biceps had no direct work all month. A month's focus will bring the curls back without crowding the legs.

focus: Keep to three workouts a week; it is working.
Break the seated row: two minutes' rest, then 3 × 10 at 130 lb.
Give the arms their due: curls back in, dips earlier.
accounts.ps: The household staff have taken to calling the leg press the master's machine. I have not discouraged them.

accounts_on_request.title: Your Grace
accounts_on_request.headline: A month of quiet progress, Your Grace, with one shoulder asking to be heard.
accounts_on_request.summary:
Ten workouts in the last thirty days, one fewer than the thirty before, but heavier ones: the leg press reached 320 lb and the pull-up is down to 70 lb of help, both new bests. The chest press made 130 lb for ten.

The shoulders are the matter of the month. Their sets halved, the lateral raise slipped from 20 lb to 15 lb, and your note of Oct 23 says the shoulder grumbled. I would rather we listened now than later.

(This is the sample household: in your own ledger the accounts are drawn from your real workouts.)
highlights: Leg press: 320 lb for 9, a new best.
Pull-up: 70 lb of help, the least yet.
Curls are back: the first in six weeks.

balance.note: Still the pride of the household.
Nine sets, down from eighteen, and a grumble on record.
The new curl is a start.

stalls.cause: The weight went to 20 lb before the reps were secure, and the shoulder has complained since.
stalls.remedy: 15 lb, slowly, until all three sets reach 12 without complaint. Then 17.5 lb.

stalls.cause: Seven sessions at 130 lb; the rest between sets is still about a minute.
stalls.remedy: Two weeks at 120 lb for 3 × 10 with two minutes' rest, then back to 130 lb.

trainer_settings.why: Trainer then chooses kinder pressing and raising for a while, without dropping the shoulders altogether.
The heavy machines want longer than the 60 seconds Trainer allows now.

focus: Mind the shoulder: lighter raises, done slowly.
Break the row with a fortnight at 120 lb.
Keep the leg press at 320 lb until all sets reach 10.
accounts_on_request.ps: I have moved the dumbbells you favour to the lower rack. It seemed the least I could do.
